summary: The templates component (templates.rs, TemplateEngine) supplies compile-time embedded project scaffolds for Rust, Python, and Node.js with {{placeholder}} substitution and optional CI workflows. Its stated purpose is to give weaker models a correct starting point so they only fill blanks rather than generating structure from scratch. On the loop it is an 'act' primitive that materializes a Plan into a concrete set of files in one deterministic step, seeded by ScaffoldOptions and InterviewContext. It reshapes the loop by front-loading correctness: instead of many risky generate-verify iterations, one scaffold act produces a known-good baseline that later stages refine.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with templates read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), where scaffolding gives 4B-9B models a correct starting point and CI workflows are optionally generated.

examples.title: Materialize a Plan into a scaffold act
examples.intent: Convert an approved project plan into concrete files in one deterministic step.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: scaffold_project turns a language + ScaffoldOptions into a file set in a single act, collapsing what would be many generate iterations into one known-good transition.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the template node onto the canvas root drops a scaffold act that fans out into file nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: The template node bursts into a cluster of file chips, each labeled with its generated path.

examples.mini_scenario: The plan calls for a Rust axum API; scaffold_project emits Cargo.toml, src/main.rs, and tests in one act.
examples.pitfall: Scaffolding writes real files — gate it behind the same act confirmation as any other filesystem mutation.

examples.title: Substitute placeholders from ScaffoldOptions
examples.intent: Fill {{placeholder}} slots so the scaffold reflects the requested project.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The engine replaces {{name}}, {{description}}, {{framework}} in each Template, so the act produces project-specific files instead of a generic stub.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping a placeholder slot on the template node opens an inline editor to set its value.
touch_interaction.visual: Unfilled {{slots}} glow amber; once bound they turn solid and show the substituted value.

examples.mini_scenario: The user names the project 'my-api'; every {{name}} in Cargo.toml and main.rs resolves to my-api.
examples.pitfall: Leave no unresolved {{placeholder}} in output — an unbound slot ships broken source.

examples.title: Seed scaffold from InterviewContext
examples.intent: Use structured pre-task answers to choose template variant and options.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: InterviewContext feeds framework/qa choices into ScaffoldOptions before the act, so the reason stage shapes exactly which Template is instantiated.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the template node opens a config wheel populated from the interview answers.
touch_interaction.visual: The wheel pre-selects framework and QA profile with the interview-derived choices highlighted.

examples.mini_scenario: The interview establishes 'FastAPI, strict QA'; the scaffold act picks the Python template with strict workflows.
examples.pitfall: Don't scaffold before the interview resolves ambiguity — a wrong framework choice wastes an act.

examples.title: Attach a CI workflow to the scaffold
examples.intent: Ship the project with a working CI gate from the first commit.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: with_ci pulls the embedded rust/python/nodejs QA workflow into the file set, so the loop's verify stage has a ready gate rather than building one later.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the template node to a CI node attaches the matching workflow file.
touch_interaction.visual: A workflow chip snaps under .github/workflows with a green gate icon.

examples.mini_scenario: with_ci=true adds rust-qa.yml so the scaffolded repo runs fmt/clippy/test on first push.
examples.pitfall: Match the workflow to the language — attaching python-qa.yml to a Rust scaffold produces a failing CI.

examples.title: Select QA profile intensity
examples.intent: Set how strict the baked-in verification should be.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: qa_profile ('standard'|'strict'|'minimal') calibrates the QA schema the scaffold ships with, tuning how hard the loop's later verify stage bites.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating a dial on the template node cycles minimal → standard → strict QA.
touch_interaction.visual: The dial fills more red as strictness climbs; the QA node shows the active tier.

examples.mini_scenario: Choosing 'strict' bakes a QA schema that fails the build on any clippy warning.
examples.pitfall: Strict on a throwaway prototype stalls the loop on nits — match the profile to the task's stakes.

examples.title: Scaffold a Rust project baseline
examples.intent: Produce a compiling Rust starting point.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The Rust Cargo.toml.template plus source stubs give the loop a project that builds immediately, so the first verify pass is likely green.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the Rust template chip onto the canvas expands the standard crate layout.
touch_interaction.visual: A crab-badged cluster of Cargo.toml, src/, and tests/ nodes appears.

examples.mini_scenario: scaffold_project('rust','tool') emits a crate that 'cargo build' passes on the first act.
examples.pitfall: The embedded Cargo.toml pins an edition/MSRV — verify it matches the workspace before adding to it.

examples.title: Scaffold a Python project baseline
examples.intent: Produce a runnable Python project with pyproject.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The pyproject.toml template plus package stubs seed a valid Python layout, shortening the loop to editing rather than authoring structure.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the Python template chip lays out pyproject.toml and the package directory.
touch_interaction.visual: A snake-badged cluster with pyproject.toml and __init__ nodes appears.

examples.mini_scenario: scaffold_project('python','svc') emits pyproject.toml and a package the agent then fills.
examples.pitfall: Placeholder substitution must reach pyproject metadata, or the package ships with the template's default name.

examples.title: Scaffold a Node/TypeScript baseline
examples.intent: Produce a TS project with tooling configs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The Node template set (package.json, tsconfig, eslint, prettier, vitest) hands the loop a fully wired TS baseline in one act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the Node template chip fans out package.json plus the four config nodes.
touch_interaction.visual: A cluster with tsconfig, eslint, prettier, and vitest chips clicks into place.

examples.mini_scenario: scaffold_project('nodejs','ui') emits package.json, tsconfig.json, and vitest.config.ts together.
examples.pitfall: The configs are opinionated — reconcile eslint/prettier with any existing repo conventions.

examples.title: Reject an unknown language early
examples.intent: Fail fast when asked to scaffold a language with no template.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: scaffold_project bails on unsupported languages, so the loop doesn't enter an act that would produce nothing usable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping an unsupported-language request flashes the template node red and refuses to expand.
touch_interaction.visual: The node shows a red cross and a 'no template' tooltip instead of file chips.

examples.mini_scenario: A request to scaffold 'cobol' bails immediately, routing the loop back to reason for a supported choice.
examples.pitfall: Return a clear error, not a partial file set — a half-scaffold pollutes the workspace.

examples.title: Opt out of test directories
examples.intent: Skip test scaffolding for a minimal spike.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: with_tests=false drops the test dirs/config from the file set, trimming the act's output for a lean loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the tests toggle on the template node removes the test chip cluster.
touch_interaction.visual: Test-related chips grey out and detach from the scaffold preview.

examples.mini_scenario: A quick spike scaffolds with_tests=false, so no tests/ dir is created.
examples.pitfall: Skipping tests also weakens the verify stage — re-enable before the project matures.

examples.title: Wire framework into the scaffold
examples.intent: Pick the framework flavor of a base template.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The optional framework field steers substitution (e.g. axum vs plain), so the reason stage biases the act toward the intended stack.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the template node opens a framework picker wheel.
touch_interaction.visual: The chosen framework badge (axum/FastAPI) pins to the template node.

examples.mini_scenario: Setting framework='axum' fills the Rust template's dependency slot with axum.
examples.pitfall: A framework the base template doesn't wire for leaves dangling imports — verify the pairing exists.

examples.title: Preview the scaffold before writing
examples.intent: Let the operator inspect the file set before it hits disk.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Rendering the file map without writing lets the loop pause at verify, gating the filesystem act on approval.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the template node expands each generated file into a readable preview panel.
touch_interaction.visual: File chips show a peek of their filled content; an approve badge waits.

examples.mini_scenario: The operator spreads the scaffold, reads the rendered Cargo.toml, then approves the write.
examples.pitfall: Preview must reflect final substitution — showing raw {{placeholders}} misleads the reviewer.

examples.title: Refine a scaffold in later iterations
examples.intent: Treat the scaffold as a seed the loop iterates on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After the scaffold act, subsequent edit acts fill blanks; the template's role is to reduce the search space each later iteration explores.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking from a scaffolded file node hands it to the edit-agent node for refinement.
touch_interaction.visual: File chips gain an 'editable' outline once the scaffold settles.

examples.mini_scenario: The Rust scaffold lands; the agent then edits src/main.rs to add the requested handler.
examples.pitfall: Don't re-scaffold to change one file — that clobbers the operator's later edits.

examples.title: Attach the QA schema to the repo
examples.intent: Ship the selfware QA schema so verification is repo-local.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The embedded QA_SCHEMA_YAML is written into the scaffold, giving the loop a durable, versioned verify policy independent of the engine.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing an edge from the template to the QA node writes the schema file.
touch_interaction.visual: A policy chip anchors at the repo root with a shield icon.

examples.mini_scenario: The scaffold writes selfware-qa-schema.yaml so future runs verify against a fixed policy.
examples.pitfall: The schema tier must match qa_profile — a strict profile with a minimal schema is inconsistent.

examples.title: Scaffold at a chosen target path
examples.intent: Write the file set to an explicit directory.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: scaffold_project takes a target Path, so the act materializes files exactly where the plan intends, keeping loop state (workspace layout) predictable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the template chip onto a folder node targets that directory for the scaffold.
touch_interaction.visual: The target folder highlights; file chips nest under it on drop.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent scaffolds into ./my-api so the new crate lives beside the workspace.
examples.pitfall: Refuse to scaffold over a non-empty target unless explicitly forced — silent overwrite loses work.

examples.title: Give weak models a correct starting point
examples.intent: Reduce structural hallucination for small models.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Per the module's purpose, handing 4B-9B models a valid scaffold means the loop's reason stage only fills blanks, cutting failed-generate iterations.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the template node shows how many boilerplate decisions it removes from the model.
touch_interaction.visual: A 'search reduced' meter fills, indicating fewer degrees of freedom left to the model.

examples.mini_scenario: A 7B model that would mis-structure a crate instead edits a correct scaffold, and the build passes.
examples.pitfall: Templates constrain, not replace, reasoning — the model still must fill the domain logic correctly.

examples.title: Keep templates compile-time embedded
examples.intent: Ensure scaffolding works offline and deterministically.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: include_str! bakes every template into the binary, so the act never depends on network or disk templates, keeping the loop hermetic.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the engine node shows the embedded template inventory baked into the binary.
touch_interaction.visual: A sealed-package icon marks the engine as self-contained; no network glyph appears.

examples.mini_scenario: Offline on a plane, scaffolding still works because the templates are in the binary.
examples.pitfall: Editing a template requires a rebuild — a runtime edit to the .template file won't take effect.

examples.title: Fan a scaffold into a plan's steps
examples.intent: Let the file set define the loop's subsequent work items.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Each ScaffoldedFile with a TODO becomes a plan step, so the scaffold act directly seeds the loop's control queue.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the scaffold cluster into the plan lane creates one step per file needing work.
touch_interaction.visual: TODO-marked file chips spawn matching task nodes in the plan rail.

examples.mini_scenario: The scaffold's stub handler carries a TODO; the loop enqueues 'implement handler' as its next step.
examples.pitfall: Don't enqueue steps for files that are already complete — the scaffold's configs need no work.

examples.title: Version-align the scaffold with the workspace
examples.intent: Ensure the scaffold's toolchain matches the surrounding repo.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Before accepting the scaffold, the verify stage checks edition/MSRV/deps against the workspace, preventing a build split.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the manifest node diffs the scaffold's toolchain against the workspace.
touch_interaction.visual: Matching versions render green; mismatches flag amber for reconciliation.

examples.mini_scenario: The scaffold's edition differs from the workspace; verify flags it before the crate is added.
examples.pitfall: A silent MSRV mismatch surfaces only in CI later — catch it at scaffold verify, not on push.

examples.title: Compose a monorepo from multiple scaffolds
examples.intent: Stand up several packages under one plan.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Multiple scaffold acts under one control plan build a monorepo; the loop sequences them, each a deterministic sub-act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing edges between multiple template nodes and a shared root composes them into one workspace.
touch_interaction.visual: Several template clusters nest under a single workspace root node with shared config chips.

examples.mini_scenario: The plan scaffolds a Rust API and a Node UI under one repo, each via its own scaffold act.
examples.pitfall: Reconcile shared configs (CI, lint) across packages — duplicated conflicting workflows break CI.
